channel.description: Latest articles from The Valley Times-News (valleytimes-news.com)

item.title: Bledsoe pens 13th book
item.description: Valley author Lanny Bledsoe’s 13th novel, “Tuck Grit,” traces a River Bluff youth who becomes a WWII fighter pilot and his wartime romance; he’ll sign copies Feb. 7 at Timeless Antiques.

item.title: Kristin Nelson elected next HD38 representative
item.description: Kristin Nelson wins Alabama House District 38 special election, defeating Democrat Hazel Floyd with 84.74% of the vote to fill the remainder of former Rep. Debbie Wood’s term.

item.title: The Coffee Gin launches donation drive
item.description: The Coffee Gin in West Point is hosting a community donation drive through Feb. 15 to collect donations for the Chattahoochee Humane Society, as well as a Troup County Toiletry Drive for the Homeless that is being organized by Chatty LaGrange Women.

item.title: CONTRIBUTOR'S VIEW - Lynn Gendusa: The Veteran, God & the Super Bowl!
item.description: Is anyone ready for a happy story? How about one that could increase your faith not only in God but also in people? Or a story about winning a grand prize or a whole enchilada! I wrote a column titled “Save Those Who Saved Us” in June 2025. I hope you read it. The column begins with our friends and neighbors, Hugh and Sabrina Macdonald. item.title: CONTRIBUTOR'S VIEW - Cathy Hunt: Fire and Ice in January
item.description: A Facebook Memory popped up yesterday from early February 2025, where I posted: “January was a tough year, but we made it.” A lot of commenters had obviously also had rough months as noted in their responses. item.title: Commissioners approve one-cent sales tax extension for BOE
item.description: Chambers County commissioners extend existing one-cent sales tax to 2055 to help the school board secure funding for a mandated $85 million consolidated high school.

item.title: Protest movement reaches LaFayette
item.description: Incidents in Minnesota have sparked national protests as people react to recent acts of violence involving Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers. Similar acts of protest were discovered in LaFayette after a concerned citizen brought them to the attention of the Valley Times‑News.

item.title: Lanett approves several resolutions, hears update on airport activity
item.description: Lanett council OKs bid for new trash contract, cable and jet-fuel software deals, and a standard hangar lease agreement as traffic and fuel sales climb at Lanett Regional Airport.

item.title: Valley football players commit to the collegiate level
item.description: Valley High quarterback Caden Foreman is on his way to Miles College in Birmingham, and one of his favorite receivers, Aaden Johnson, is bound for Millsaps College in Jackson, Mississippi.

item.title: Spencer Newman commits to Murray State University
item.description: Chambers Academy’s Spencer Newman, who helped win three state titles, becomes the school’s first Division I football signee with his National Signing Day commitment to Murray State.
